title: Thoracic T4-T5 and T8-T9 absolute IDP vs follower load, rib cage stiffened (plates ribs 2-5)

quantity.name: IDP
quantity.definition: absolute nucleus pressure (mean over specimens) at static follower load 0-600 N, no moment

source.authors: Anderson DE, Mannen EM, Sis HL, Wong BM, Cadel ES, Friis EA, Bouxsein ML
source.sample: human cadaver T1-T12 thoracic spines with rib cage, fresh-frozen; 8 specimens (8 T1-T12 thoracic spines with intact rib cage); a few discs without useful pressure excluded (number not stated)

protocol.summary: Static, upright, unconstrained T1-T12 spine with rib cage; T1 and T12 potted (Bondo), T12 bolted to horizontal surface, T1 free; follower load 0/200/400/600 N via bilateral cables through rods in T3-T11 vertebral bodies (half the load hung on each cable, pulleys below T11). No applied moment. Test order: intact rib cage -> stiffened rib cage (plates bridging costal cartilage/sternocostal joints ribs 2-5) -> ribs cut lateral to costotransverse joints (No Ribs). IDP: Gaeltec side-mounted transducer on 1.3 mm needle in the centre of the nucleus of T4-T5 and T8-T9 (radiograph-confirmed), 10 Hz, averaged static value; absolute pressure.
how_to_simulate: Model T1-T12 with rib cage (or without, per condition); fix T12 inferior endplate; leave T1 free (no moment).
Apply a follower load along the curvature (cables through T3-T11 vertebral bodies, anchored at T1 potting) of 0, 200, 400, 600 N.
Read absolute nucleus pressure at the centre of the T4-T5 and T8-T9 discs at each load step.
protocol.notes: Authors state testing order (intact always first) likely confounds rib-cage effects; pressure-follower slope 1.24 kPa/N (T4-T5) and 1.00 kPa/N (T8-T9) intact (Table 1). No Ribs T4-T5 at 0 N recorded as 0 kPa (at/below sensor minimum) in all specimens (text).
